summary: The LED savings calculator turns the price, the lifetime and more into reg bulb 1yr cost. That makes it useful for a practical question that turns up in daily life. The results leave the screen the moment you edit a field; press Calculate and they come back updated, so a single changed input shows its own effect.

sections.title: How does the LED savings calculator work?
sections.html:
The LED savings calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports reg bulb 1yr cost in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the bulb type); then you type in the price (LED bulb), the lifetime (LED bulb), the daily usage and over how many years?.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the LED savings calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Reg bulb 1yr cost=(487 ÷ 4800000) × daily usage × energy price × power consumption + price × rounded up, ((1461 ÷ 4) × daily usage ÷ lifetime)
Price=(-487 ÷ 4800000 × daily usage × energy price × over how many years? × power consumption + regular bulb total cost) ÷ rounded up, ((1461 ÷ 4) × daily usage × over how many years? ÷ lifetime)
Power consumption=(4800000 ÷ 487) × (LED bulb 1yr cost − price × rounded up, ((1461 ÷ 4) × daily usage ÷ lifetime)) ÷ (daily usage × energy price)
Power consumption=(4800000 ÷ 487) × (-price × rounded up, ((1461 ÷ 4) × daily usage × over how many years? ÷ lifetime) + LED total cost) ÷ (daily usage × energy price × over how many years?)
Break even after=(31557600 × LED bulb 1yr cost ÷ reg bulb 1yr cost)
Price=(-487 ÷ 48000 × daily usage × energy price × power consumption + reg bulb 100yr cost) ÷ rounded up, ((7305 ÷ 2) × daily usage ÷ lifetime)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Power, opening in watts
  • Time, opening in hours
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Power, opening in watts
  • Time, opening in hours
  • Time, opening in seconds
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The LED savings calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the price, the lifetime and the daily usage — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the LED savings calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns reg bulb 1yr cost, derived from the price, the lifetime and the daily usage. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the LED savings calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the price, the lifetime, the daily usage and over how many years?, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter price (LED bulb) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Price (LED bulb) opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Power consumption = 60 W. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the LED savings calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
